candidates.title: Sound-installation as retail placemaking device
candidates.shift: Interactive public sound/confession installations are appearing as art pieces that create shared, ambient community experience in built spaces.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could point to a next wave of 'experience infrastructure' — anonymous, ambient, sensory installations used to build community feel in retail/public space, distinct from screens or events.
candidates.evidence: Coletivo 624's 'Raconte-moi un secret' invites public sharing of anonymous confessions as a collective soundscape.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from purely visual/digital store experience toward anonymous, ambient sound-based community engagement. If adopted in commercial contexts, retailers might build 'confession booths' or soundscapes as a differentiator for physical presence over eComm.
candidates.author: Susanna Moreira

candidates.title: Wearable recovery tech entering 'Future Stadium' infrastructure
candidates.shift: Sportswear and health-tech companies are embedding heat/vibration recovery devices into everyday wearables (slides), tied explicitly to stadium/venue experience design.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative/Hype: named product already covered by trade press, but worth watching for how physical-AI wearables extend into retail/stadium environments as an infrastructure layer, not just a product.
candidates.evidence: Nike and Hyperice unveiled heated, vibrating slides as part of a 'Future Stadium' series on Dezeen.
candidates.initial_analysis: Already-named product launch; included for context. Points toward physical-AI wearables becoming part of venue/stadium 'infrastructure' narratives, which could eventually touch how retail/sport venues design recovery or comfort zones.
candidates.author: Tom Ravenscroft

candidates.title: Empty-nest downsizing reshaping suburban lot choices
candidates.shift: Couples with grown children are choosing smaller, well-sited lots over larger family homes, prioritizing optimized lifestyle over square footage.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a demographic signal — if downsizing scales, it could shift suburban housing stock composition and nearby retail catchment density/formats over the next decade.
candidates.evidence: Jabuticabeiras House (Goiânia, Brazil) built at 361m² on a smaller lot after owners' children moved out, described as strategic downsizing.
candidates.initial_analysis: Single instance of an emerging empty-nester downsizing pattern in Latin America. If widespread, could shrink average household footprint and shift suburban retail catchment sizing and format mix over H3.
candidates.author: Susanna Moreira

candidates.title: Regionally-sourced craft materials in new-build farmhouses
candidates.shift: New residential builds are explicitly drawing on local craftsmanship and regional building traditions rather than imported/standardized materials.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a small but recurring reframing — regional material sourcing as a construction-supply-chain response to cost/climate pressures, worth tracking for retail-adjacent construction too.
candidates.evidence: NUA Arquitectures' Casa Juià in Catalonia uses regional craftsmanship and local material wrapping for a farmhouse near Gavarres mountains.
candidates.initial_analysis: Single residential instance of regional-materials-first construction; if this scales it could inform supply-chain localization for commercial builds seeking resilience and lower embodied carbon.
candidates.author: Ariane Shah

candidates.title: Adaptive reuse under strict historic-district zoning
candidates.shift: Older buildings in historic districts are being modernized internally while preserving stringent exterior regulations, a template for constrained adaptive reuse.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: as more mass-market retail eyes older/urban infill sites, this kind of tight-zoning adaptive-reuse playbook (modern interior, preserved shell) may become a template for constrained urban stores.
candidates.evidence: LBWA's renovation of a 1930s villa in Poznań's Grunwald district was constructed and now renovated under stringent original development regulations.
candidates.initial_analysis: A single residential case of zoning-constrained adaptive reuse; relevant as a construction/policy template for retailers seeking historic-district footholds where new-build zoning is restrictive.
candidates.author: Pratik Mour

candidates.title: Commercial-to-residential conversion of niche hospitality space
candidates.shift: Former specialty commercial/hospitality facilities (e.g. a mezcal tasting room) are being converted into residential use rather than remaining commercial.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a small counter-signal to commercial-to-residential retail conversion trend generally discussed — worth flagging as evidence the reverse direction (niche hospitality to housing) is also occurring in dense urban cores like Mexico City.
candidates.evidence: Casa Mezcal in La Condesa, Mexico City, transforms a former mezcal tasting facility into a contemporary family residence.
candidates.initial_analysis: Single instance of commercial-to-residential conversion in a Latin American urban core; useful as a rule-out or counter-example to watch against the more common residential/office-to-retail conversion narrative.
candidates.author: Cristina Popescu

candidates.title: Real-estate marketing 'show villas' repurposed into commercial renewal districts
candidates.shift: Former villa show/model homes built for real-estate marketing are being clustered and converted into a commercial urban-renewal node rather than demolished.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative and peripheral (China): reframes throwaway marketing real-estate (show villas) as a reusable commercial asset class — an absence/category not yet named in Western retail real estate (adaptive reuse of sales-center structures).
candidates.evidence: Luxe Lakes CPI Island in Chengdu repurposes more than 20 former villa show models into a commercial renewal project on Luke Island.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from disposable real-estate marketing structures (show villas) to permanent commercial reuse — a genuinely novel adaptive-reuse category. If it spreads, developers elsewhere may start designing sales centers for post-sale commercial afterlives, changing how show-home capital is amortized.
candidates.author: Andreas Luco

candidates.title: Mass-timber construction stretched to tight-budget public buildings
candidates.shift: Mass-timber structural systems, once a premium material choice, are being used for budget-constrained public buildings (schools) prioritizing healthy materials over spectacle.
candidates.ai_read: Trend/Signal: mass timber adoption is increasingly covered, but its move into cost-constrained public typologies (vs flagship commercial) suggests broader viability for mass-market retail construction seeking low-carbon, faster builds.
candidates.evidence: Martin Hopp Architect completed Evergreen Charter School in Hempstead, NY using mass-timber structure on a tight budget, opened 2025.
candidates.initial_analysis: Mass timber's structural/cost story is already trending, included for context. Its use in budget-constrained public buildings is the interesting edge — suggests retailers could adopt mass timber for cost-sensitive store builds, not just flagship projects.
candidates.author: Kate Mazade
